Meeting header
Date: 2025-11-23 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Links shared: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk-quickstart, https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts/tree/main/sandbox, https://drive.company/blueanchor/traffic-profile (customer)

Summary:
Short live workshop to walk BlueAnchor through SDK auth flow (Python + TS), KMS integration options for API keys, sandbox creds provisioning, and an Optimize checklist for batching + caching. Aim: get a dev onramp + schedule perf baseline.

Topics covered:
- SDK auth env vars and secrets rotation
- KMS/HSM integration patterns (bring-your-own KMS vs Redwood-managed)
- Sandbox provisioning and quickstart repo pairing (Py/TS)
- Console walkthrough for keys, roles, and RBAC
- Redwood Optimize tips: batching, prefix/KV cache, quantization guidance
- Next steps: pricing + benchmark scheduling

Action items (captured verbally during call):
- Samira to send pricing & KMS architecture note
- Jorge to spin up sandbox account and post repo link
- Ari to share traffic profile and SSO metadata for SAML test

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira Patel: Alright everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Samira from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account, with me is Jorge and Maya. How are you folks doing?
[00:10] Ari Kwan: Good, thanks. Ready to go. We got Lena and Devon on our side.
[00:15] Lena Ortiz: Hey all. Trying to get this on the calendar for our infra team.
[00:22] Jorge Alvarez: Cool, quick agenda — we'll do a live SDK pairing, show auth env setup for both Python and TypeScript, then look at KMS options, and finish with an Optimize checklist. Sound ok?
[00:30] Devon Price: Yep, sounds good. We're particularly interested in KMS and key rotation — must be HIPAA-ready-ish.
[00:36] Samira Patel: Yep totally, we'll show both Redwood-managed KMS and the BYO KMS flow, and how keys rotate. Also show how to restrict tokens via RBAC on the console.
[00:45] Ari Kwan: Also curious about dedicated vs hosted — our compliance team, if we go hosted data residency and audit logs are must-haves.
[00:50] Maya Chen: We'll cover that. Quick callout — Redwood has Private with VPC/on-prem options, and Dedicated reserved pools, both include audit log hooks and KMS integration.

[02:00] (screen share starts)
[02:15] Jorge Alvarez: I'm pulling up the Python quickstart. First thing is set your env var REDWOOD_API_KEY, we usually recommend ephemeral keys backed by KMS if you want rotation. Example snippet: export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk-.." then pip install redwood-sdk.
[02:35] Devon Price: For the TS side where do you store that in CI? We're on CircleCI and GitHub actions.
[02:40] Jorge Alvarez: Same pattern — store the key in secrets manager (GH secrets / Circle env), then inject at runtime. If you're BYO KMS, you can use a CI plugin to decrypt at job runtime. We also showed a sample GH actions file in the quickstart repo.

[05:10] Lena Ortiz: Quick question — we need SSO and SAML for console access, what's the setup?
[05:15] Maya Chen: You upload SAML metadata to the Redwood Console under Settings -> SSO. You can map groups to roles for RBAC. There's a couple of gotchas — group names must match exactly when you map, and Roles are, um, case sensitive in the console today.
[05:30] Ari Kwan: Ok. Does key rotation break running inference? Like sessions with KV cache, does cache invalidation happen?
[05:38] Jorge Alvarez: Good question — rotating the API key does not evict KV cache in the runtime, because KV is tied to model session id not API key; however if you rotate keys and also re-provision a different tenant, you'll want to coordinate prefix cache invalidation. There's a docs note about 'prefix/KV caching' under Optimize.

[08:00] (pair-programming, Jorge types live)
[08:12] Jorge Alvarez: On the Python example — from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) — simple. For streaming, use client.stream() and handle partial tokens.
[08:30] Devon Price: Is there a typed SDK for TS?
[08:33] Jorge Alvarez: Yes, the TypeScript SDK is strongly typed. import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood-inference/sdk'; const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); We linked the d.ts in the repo.

[11:10] Lena Ortiz: On KMS, can we bring our AWS KMS CMKs? We need HSM-backed keys.
[11:16] Maya Chen: Yep. Two patterns — BYO-KMS where you store an encrypted wrapper token in your vault and Redwood fetches it via a connector, or Redwood-managed keys stored in our HSM offering. BYO gives you direct key control and rotations; Redwood-managed is easier and available with enterprise contracts. Both support audit logs.
[11:38] Ari Kwan: If we do BYO, what does the vault connector look like?
[11:42] Jorge Alvarez: It's a small daemon or a short-lived credential exchange — we gave a sample implementation that polls your KMS for a wrapped key and unwraps into an ephemeral token. We can share the repo snippet. It's in the quickstart under /kms.

[15:05] (brief crosstalk, host mutes background)
[15:20] Devon Price: For prod, what's the token TTL you recommend? We don't want to rotate every minute.
[15:25] Maya Chen: Typical pattern: issue short-lived tokens for compute nodes (15-60m) and longer lived management tokens for CI/CD with stricter RBAC. We recommend 1-hour TTL for worker nodes. If you use prefix caching and batching, short TTLs are fine because they don't affect the model's KV cache.

[18:00] Jorge Alvarez: Now onto the console — creating a service role: Settings -> API -> Create service token -> scope: models:invoke, logs:read. You can pin tokens to a route and restrict by IP if needed.
[18:22] Lena Ortiz: Can we limit token to only the dev sandbox?
[18:25] Jorge Alvarez: Yep, you scope by project/env. We'll provision a sandbox project for BlueAnchor so tokens are scoped.

[21:40] Samira Patel: Quick Optimize notes — for chat-heavy workflows, enable continuous batching, set batch size to match your p95 latency target, and enable prefix cache on common prompts. That reduces token costs significantly.
[21:58] Devon Price: How does quantization come into play? We run 8-bit quant models in prod to save costs.
[22:04] Maya Chen: Redwood supports quantized variants; the runtime picks quant kernels depending on model and hardware. We'll recommend a model/quant profile after we see your payload distribution. Optimize's recommendation engine can propose quantization for throughput vs quality tradeoffs.

[27:00] (screen shows sample request/response)
[27:15] Jorge Alvarez: Example request — POST /v1/generate with headers Authorization: Bearer <REDWOOD_API_KEY> and body {model: 'redwood-1.2x', input: 'Summarize...'}. For streaming in TS we show an EventSource wrapper in the quickstart.
[27:45] Devon Price: Any rate limits we should know?
[27:48] Jorge Alvarez: Hosted accounts have default rate limits, and Dedicated gives you reserved throughput. For sandbox we'll turn off aggressive limits but production you'll get per-second quotas which we can size in the sales quote.

[31:50] Lena Ortiz: On audit logs — we need per-request user identifier with SSO mapping. Can Redwood attach a user_id to each request for compliance?
[31:58] Maya Chen: Yes, you can include x-redwood-user header with the SSO-mapped user id; audit logs will show that field. We can also ship CloudTrail-style export or a webhook for logs.

[34:10] Ari Kwan: Let's talk timeline — we want a small pilot in Q1, maybe January. What's realistic for sandbox -> pilot -> prod?
[34:18] Samira Patel: Typical path: sandbox (1–2 weeks), pilot with perf baseline (2–4 weeks), then production (4–8 weeks) depending on compliance and procurement. For BlueAnchor, compliance gating might add time, but we can run a dedicated private deployment earlier if needed.

[36:00] (walkthrough of quickstart repo)
[36:12] Jorge Alvarez: Repo includes: /py-quickstart, /ts-quickstart, /kms, /saml-sample, and a runbook for perf tests. We'll drop the sandbox credentials in the shared drive and give repo access.
[36:28] Devon Price: Can we get a sample traffic profile template?
[36:30] Samira Patel: We'll attach a Google Sheet template — send us your p50/p95 latency and token distribution and we'll use it to size Dedicated.

[40:44] (customer asks about fallback)
[40:50] Maya Chen: We have smart routing — you can set policy to fall back to a cheaper model variant if a primary is unavailable. Also automatic retries for transient infra errors.

[43:30] Lena Ortiz: Any gotchas we should watch for in initial integration?
[43:36] Jorge Alvarez: Watch for environment mismatch — node vs python where newline handling or streaming event parsing differs. Also check that your CI secrets are set for both test and prod. And beware that proper mapping of SAML groups to console roles saves a lot of headaches later.

[46:00] (wrap-up)
[46:10] Samira Patel: Recap — we'll: 1) provision sandbox and share repo + creds (Jorge), 2) Samira sends pricing + KMS note, 3) Ari sends traffic profile and SSO metadata. We'll schedule a 30-minute perf run with Jorge on Nov 28 to baseline. Does that work?
[46:30] Ari Kwan: Yes looks good.
[46:34] Devon Price: One last Q — does Redwood store prompts or PII by default?
[46:40] Maya Chen: By default, hosted will keep logs for X days depending on plan; you can opt-in to no-log mode or use Private deployment to keep everything in your VPC. We will share the data retention options in the security doc.

[49:00] Samira Patel: Ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links.
[49:05] (meeting ends)
